notes.title: JULY 2025 - PROGRESS UPDATE
notes.content:
[p]This post is mirrored from our [url="https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/holohammer/mindwave/posts/4444993"]recent Kickstarter update[/url], and omits details about physical backer rewards.[/p][p][/p][p]Hello! It's been a little bit since the last update, and we've got some good stuff to share!
Let's jump into what we've been up to with MINDWAVE since the end of the Kickstarter campaign.[/p][p][/p][p]This update is written by both Megalo (Director + Main Artist) and mook (Project Manager + Systems Programmer).[/p][p][/p][h3][b]POST-KICKSTARTER BUSINESS[/b][/h3][p]👽 mook:
Our first priority was to figure out the business end of things. I sent out backer surveys, organized backer info, allowed backers with declined payments to pledge after the campaign, answered a bunch of Kickstarter messages, sorted out legal business, split the money up into different sub-budgets, and set up the ability to get ourselves paid.[/p][p]This business stuff was easy on paper, but it was our first time ever doing this kind of thing, so it ended up a little more daunting once it was actually in front of us. It was a lot for all of us to figure out together, but we got through it![/p][p]Beyond business stuff, I fixed some bugs for the demo (the last patch was in April, and there may be even more bugs to fix?), and I helped manage our fan art contest. I set up the Google Form for voting, and I put together the winner announcement video. I also worked with the talented [u][url="https://bsky.app/profile/krz.rocks"]krz[/url][/u] to make a bot to automatically(-ish) distribute roles to Kickstarter backers in our [u][url="https://holohammer.com/discord"]Discord server[/url][/u].[/p][p][/p][h3][b]MINDWAVE, MIND 2, AND MORE[/b][/h3][p]
🌙 Megalo:
After the dust settled with business and post-Kickstarter work, we jumped right into development for the second minigame set in the game, Mind 2! Mind 2 was a weird one for a while. I always knew the general look and sound I wanted for this character’s minigame set, and a vague idea of what they represented to me. Until more recently, Mind 2 was always on the back burner in my mind.[/p][p]Over the years, I had small concept doodles/ideas here and there, but what I wanted really started to click recently once we finally fully jumped in. Me and our gameplay programmer Milkshake have been working together to complete a bunch of the minigames for Mind 2, with my art and her implementation/added visual flair. Everything's been coming out great! With the work that’s gone into it, Mind 2 is already looking to be something really exciting![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/da8727b5c50c13c1157f0e9c8c461a6a7ba4fc94.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/f01270cc2e8735473805024252273f311f0d8aa2.png"][/img][/p][p]🌙 Megalo:
In regards to the music for Mind 2, our musician Dorkus made 3 separate demos to try and nail the sound. The third one ended up being the one that fit really well for what we wanted, and he's in the middle of finishing it right now![/p][p]He’s been super awesome to work with and his musical range is super flexible, I think people will really like it when they play the stage and hear it. As for the other 2 scrapped demos, perhaps we’ll show them later down the line after the game is out?[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/2c5e851fddbe43d067503bbbeb858ad44a09f7b4.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/df544a6e273aeda170f933b3bc8427b506d6b96b.png"][/img][/p][p]🌙 Megalo:
The way that we've decided to approach the game right now is developing each Minigame set/Mind until they're in a passable alpha state. With the alpha state, not everything's finished and some minigames are missing, but it's playable and the main idea/tone is there.
After we finish getting into this alpha state for a minigame set, we move onto the next! This is to get us a big picture idea of the entire game/the flow of everything as early as possible, kinda like sketching out a big illustration to make sure the composition feels right before getting into more detail.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/c64f94d337ca24c56941cf0dfc936c75916b93e4.gif"][/img][/p][p]Right now we're finishing up Mind 2’s alpha state, and are easing into work for Mind 3! I’ve already been refining old concepts for Mind 3 on the side, and have been fleshing out the character with the writers! The process of making a minigame set has sped up a ton compared to where we were with Starlight (Mind 1) after the same amount of development time, and we’re proud of how far we’ve come with that![/p][p][/p][p]🌙 Megalo:
As for other stuff I've worked on besides Kickstarter/Mind 2 work, I’ve updated some old moodboards for the other stages in the game, and I've thrown together some mockup/concept videos for some Minds and moments later in the game when inspiration strikes, in order to communicate the tone I wanna go for with them to the team. I've also fleshed out concept art for some of the other lobby floors in the game, designed some new faces to encounter in the lobby segments, and done some fleshing out of major story beats…[/p][p]
Speaking of the game's narrative! Me, mook, and our writers Starmy/Mizu have had a lot of meetings and talks about MINDWAVE’s story and characters, and a branch of what we've discussed is rethinking how we wanna approach writing the lobbies. We gave the writing a lot of attention to be ready for the demo, and we were happy a lot of people seemed to enjoy the narrative segments of the game![/p][p]But at the same time the demo was a great opportunity to shine a light on flaws we saw with these segments. It's a different experience watching regular people play the stuff you make, it puts stuff through a different lens. So without saying too much, Starmy and Mizu have been working on fleshing out how we approach each lobby to be more focused, and it’s already felt like it's been paying off!

With the lobbies we're also experimenting a bit on the side in a different way with the help of a secret buddy of ours.... and it's looking pretty neat..... we'll have to see how it feels when it's done, though.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/25d740bd99e85e51f02a638f8e0d4faa541e6e9d.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]🌙 Megalo:
In terms of the story's big picture, it’s been shaping up to be something really special to me. Very early on in MINDWAVE’s development in 2023, I was unsure of what I wanted out of the game’s narrative, only knowing what major moments I wanted to include. The game was still very much an expression of myself and the things I loved but a lot of the details were blurry.[/p][p]There was a point where I wasn’t really too concerned with how we presented the game outside of the minigame sets themselves. However, over the course of the demo's development, and even more as time went on, I found more ways to express myself through the narrative, and also put more of myself into the minigame sets. As time went on I became really attached to the games narrative and am [i]really[/i] excited about the direction we have.
Part of this was because of my own major breakthroughs in how I thought about the game, but I feel like I also owe a lot of it to Starmy and Mizu for helping me flesh out the ideas I had, filling in the gaps between these major moments, and making it all make sense. They’re really fantastic at what they do, and help me know what I want out of the game’s story, and make me look at things differently in ways that make the experience of the game feel more personal overall![/p][p][/p][h3][b]SYSTEM REWORKS[/b][/h3][p]👽 mook:
As for some of the more technical programming-y details, I've got some cool things to share.[/p][p]I've started work on some big system reworks that'll allow the game to be made better and faster. Right now I'm working on what I call the "metagame system." It's built from scratch based on the best parts of the existing minigame system, and it works like an "engine-within-an-engine" that allows us to quickly swap between lightweight "scenes" which we use for both minigames and the "inbetween" score animations.[/p][p]It can all run on a timeline that we place events on, similar to a video editing software. Here's what that looks like.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/705f064f48bb53230c77d285274568b4c20377a0.gif"][/img][/p][p]👽 mook:
While scenes have been functional for a while, the timeline system is still a bit new, so some of the visuals/functionality shown here are in-progress. Incorrect control prompt, no minigame command, no early finish for the minigames, etc.[/p][p][b]Metagame:[/b] Controls the scoring and keeps track of certain variables between minigames
[b]Timeline:[/b] Manages the order and timing of events (including minigames + inbetweens)
[b]Scenes:[/b] The new system (based on the old minigame system) that minigames + inbetweens will be running on. Lightweight and self-contained![/p][p]Scenes are written with full backwards-compatibility with the old minigame system, so new minigames can still be programmed for the old system while the metagame system is in progress! It's important that big system reworks don't slow down the game's development.[/p][p]The goal of the metagame/timeline/scene system is to allow us more freedom in how we make the game. The old system (which is present in the demo) was very rigid, and forced a specific flow between minigames and inbetweens, which meant that when we wanted to switch things up (such as with "Combo Time"), we had to jump through a lot of hoops to get those out-there ideas working.
Now that the system is opening up more, we'll have a lot more creative freedom to switch things up.[/p][p]There's some other stuff on my systems implementation list, such as FMOD (as mentioned in a previous update), but we'll have to wait a little while before I can share the specifics there. I haven't even finished the metagame system yet! One step at a time.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]DIEBACK[/b][/h3][p]👽 mook: 
Dieback is a tool made by our friend Okano that lets you make your own EarthBound-esque wavy visuals using an artist-friendly interface with layers and sliders (since visuals like this usually have to be made by a programmer).[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/1eea37ffbb1ce80788d064bc42e6c278076b6339.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]background of our new game over screen[/i][/p][p]👽 mook:
Dieback has been used a lot by Megalo throughout MINDWAVE's development to conceptualize certain visuals like the background of the main menu. The biggest issue has been that there wasn't direct GameMaker support for it, so we had to manually adjust the numbers for our own shaders until the result looked close enough to whatever mockup Megalo made using Dieback. [/p][p]At a few points we had to compromise getting some backgrounds accurate to the mockups since it was time consuming (we spent multiple hours recreating Megalo's Dieback mockup for the main menu background).
Well, thanks to our pestering (lol), Okano has created a Dieback port for GameMaker! This means we'll be able to have Megalo's Dieback mockups no longer just be mockups! cool.
[i](just kidding it wasn't actually pestering, okano worked on it after i asked once. it was awesome)[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/9a765423cc8733dc8b8bbf4c9a372cd08e067723.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]"STITCH" microgame background as originally intended[/i][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/d8a6b18fcd7a071650626ea9539344b7a97a7af4.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]"CATCH" microgame background as originally intended[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Both Dieback and its GameMaker port are free, so you can use them too! [/p][p]Check out [u][url="https://okano.itch.io/dieback"]Dieback on itch.io[/url][/u] and give [u][url="https://bsky.app/profile/oxee.io"]Okano's Bluesky[/url][/u] a follow if you'd like![/p][p][/p][p]For info on our physical backer rewards, read [url="https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/holohammer/mindwave/posts/4444993"]this post on Kickstarter![/url][/p][p][/p][h3][b]UNTIL NEXT TIME[/b][/h3][p]🌙 Megalo:
That all being said, that's gonna be it for this update. We wanted to wait to have all the merch stuff ready before posting this, so it's a bit of a big update! All of us on the MINDWAVE team are really excited for what's to come with the game and we're really proud of the direction we've been in recently. None of it would be possible without the support of backers and followers of the game, so thank you guys so much![/p][p]Until next time![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44795746/19d0e87fdc21f68050f70d66d32905073f6e3fab.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Demo v1.0.3 Patch Notes
notes.content:
A demo patch has been released! Your title screen should say [b]Demo v1.0.3[/b]. If it doesn't, you can verify demo files to force the update. (Game Settings -> Properties -> Installed Files -> Verify integrity of demo files)

This should be the final demo patch for the foreseeable future (barring very minor bug fixes) as we fully shift our focus to making further progress on the full game.

Here's what we changed:
[h3]Miscellaneous[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added Top 3 Local scores display to Mind Select menu
[*] Enabled Steam Cloud saves
[*] Previously, if your game profile got corrupted, the game would crash on startup. Now a message displays to tell you your profile is corrupted, then you can continue to the game. A corrupt profile will reset settings and playtime, but will have Mind Select unlocked. Story Mode progress and high scores will not be reset.
[*] Fixed various menu crashes that could result from frame-perfect escape key presses
[*] Fixed crashes involving invalid Steam profile pictures displaying in the leaderboard.
[*] All dialogue strings and other hardcoded strings were moved to lang.json
[/list]
[h3]Microgames[/h3]
[list]
[*] After thorough testing, we can confirm that the speed cap for endless mode is now where we intend it to be. Regular Endless speed caps at 2.18x, and Simple Endless speed caps at 3x.
[*] Fixed a bug where toggling Simple Mode and then playing Standard (story) Starlight would cause the popups to not appear after the speed up/level up.
[/list]
[b]Starlight[/b]
TRANSFORM!
[list]
[*] Made the beginning input grace period slightly shorter
[/list]
[b]Tutorial[/b]
CIRCLE!
[list]
[*] Improved collision accuracy on the circle
[*] Decreased the volume of the win sound effect
[/list]
If you still have issues with any of the problems we claim to have fixed, let us know in the community discussions forum :)

notes.title: Demo v1.0.2 Patch Notes
notes.content:
A demo patch has been released! Your title screen should say [b]Demo v1.0.2[/b]. If it doesn't, you can verify demo files to force the update. (Game Settings -> Properties -> Installed Files -> Verify integrity of demo files)

Here's what we changed:
[h3]Miscellaneous[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed a crash that can happen at the end of an Endless run
[*] Fixed a white flash that can happen after playing Standard Starlight from Mind Select
[*] Adjusted April Herndon's role in the credits to be more clear
[*] Adjusted difficulty balancing in Endless mode: harder versions of some microgames should be more common now, and will become more common the longer you play
[*] Fixed a crash that could happen when opening the dialogue log while [spoiler]Dom is showing you his song[/spoiler]
[*] Fixed the dialogue log's scrollbar jumping up if you kept holding down the mouse button after dragging the scrollbar and then closing the log
[*] Adjusted an engine setting that may have been preventing some devices from saving and loading (if you were having trouble with this, let us know if this helped!)
[/list]
[h3]Microgames[/h3]
[b]Starlight[/b]
BRUSH!
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where the hair can go back to being messy even after winning the microgame
[/list]
PADDLE!
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where you can hit the ball after losing the microgame
[/list]
AVOID!
[list]
[*] Made the heart semi-transparent to signal a certain mechanic
[*] Made the microgame harder at higher game speeds
[/list]
DROP!
[list]
[*] Fixed a crash that could occur when stacking pieces too high
[/list]
JUMP!
[list]
[*] Various changes to the player animations to hopefully make the controls clearer to first-time players
[*] Fixed a bug where you can jump after losing the microgame
[*] Fixed a visual bug near the top of the level
[*] Fixed a bug where an unintended sound effect can play after winning the microgame
[/list]

[b]Tutorial[/b]
CIRCLE!
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where the first line you draw couldn't be as long as normal
[*] Drawing a line at max length will now count as an attempted closed circle instead of cancelling
[*] Decreased the line's max length
[*] Fixed a crash involving the line being too long
[/list]
CATCH! (Demon)
[list]
[*] The demon now flies around in a shorter area as game speed increases
[/list]

[b]Shuffle[/b]
SWIPE!
[list]
[*] Changed prompt from SWIPE! to PUSH!
[*] Downward mouse movement no longer reverses progress (temporary fix while we determine how to make the required mouse movement more clear to players)
[*] Fixed a crash involving the inverse kinematics on the arms
[/list]

If you still have issues with any of the problems we claim to have fixed, let us know in the community discussions forum :)

notes.title: Demo v1.0.1 Patch Notes
notes.content:
A demo patch has been released! Your title screen should say [b]Demo v1.0.1[/b]. If it doesn't, you can verify demo files to force the update. (Game Settings -> Properties -> Installed Files -> Verify integrity of demo files)

Here's what we changed:
[list]
[*] Raised max speed for Simple Endless mode
[*] TUG! microgame prompt changed to SWIPE!
[*] Added an arrow indicator to the mouse animation in SWIPE! (previously TUG!)
[*] The opening cutscene can now be skipped with the spacebar (previously only the escape key)
[*] Hopefully disabled the bits of code that were causing the game to get flagged by antivirus programs. If you had issues with this, let us know how it goes!
[*] Added underlines to dialogue options to make them distinct from standard text
[*] Fixes crashes related to transitions in the main menu
[*] Fixed the crash that happened when opening the leaderboard or playing endless mode immediately after beating story mode
[*] Fixed friends leaderboard tab not starting with #1 rank
[*] Fixed a crash involving the leaderboard that could occur at the end of an endless run
[*] Made Steam's screenshot key work (F12 for most people)
[/list]

If you still have issues with any of the problems we claim to have fixed, let us know in the community discussions forum :)
